questions.q: Spot the error: (a) In science the credit goes to a man / (b) who convinces the world / (c) not to the man to whom / (d) the idea first occurs. / (e) No error.
options: In science the credit goes to a man
not to the man to whom
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct correlative conjunction pair is 'not... but'. It should be 'but to the man to whom'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) It is only after / (b) the war is over / (c) that people realise / (d) how bad it was. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Tense consistency is required. Since the main clause uses present tense ('is', 'realise'), the subordinate clause should also be in present tense: 'how bad it is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Of the two / (b) answers, this / (c) is definitely / (d) better. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Of the two' correctly takes the comparative degree 'better'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He is unfortunate enough / (b) to lose / (c) few friends he made / (d) during his stay at Patna. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When referring to specific friends he made, the definite article is required. It should be 'the few friends he made'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) There were a number / (b) of pretty girls in the party / (c) but it was Ragini / (d) who remained a centre of attraction. / (e) No error.
options: of pretty girls in the party
who remained a centre of attraction.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When someone is the unique or primary focus of attention, the definite article 'the' is used. It should be 'the centre of attraction'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) I have been / (b) informed that / (c) Dr. Sinha visits Patna / (d) the following month. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In reported speech or future reference from a past perspective, 'the next month' is the standard phrasing, not 'the following month' in this specific context, or 'visits' should be 'will visit the following month'. However, the classic error here is 'the following month' should be 'the next month' when shifting from 'next month' in direct speech.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He is / (b) the best artist / (c) of the time but unfortunately / (d) least recognised. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Superlative adjectives must be preceded by the definite article 'the'. It should be 'the least recognised'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He said that he felt nervous / (b) because a friend of his / (c) had given him / (d) a very bad news. / (e) No error.
options: He said that he felt nervous
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and cannot take the indefinite article 'a'. It should be 'very bad news' or 'a piece of very bad news'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) I don't like / (b) that type of a man / (c) who does nothing but / (d) find out faults in others. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: After 'type of', 'kind of', or 'sort of', the indefinite article 'a/an' is not used. It should be 'that type of man'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He claims to be a linguist / (b) but, in reality, he / (c) does not know even / (d) the A B C of linguistics. / (e) No error.
options: He claims to be a linguist
the A B C of linguistics.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'The ABC of' is a standard idiomatic expression meaning the basics.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The remedy lies / (b) in promoting values of humanism / (c) and democracy so as to combat / (d) the oncoming brand of fascism. / (e) No error.
options: and democracy so as to combat
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'values' is followed by 'of', it requires the definite article. It should be 'the values of humanism'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) When the house was / (b) set on the fire, all the people / (c) started crying at the top / (d) of their voices. / (e) No error.
options: set on the fire, all the people
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct idiomatic phrase is 'set on fire', without the article 'the'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) A first step / (b) in a rational solution / (c) to any problem is / (d) the recognition of the fact that a problem exists. / (e) No error.
options: the recognition of the fact that a problem exists.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When referring to the initial step in a specific process, the definite article is used. It should be 'The first step'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Little knowledge / (b) of music that he possessed / (c) proved to be a boon for him / (d) when he was utterly helpless. / (e) No error.
options: proved to be a boon for him
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Because the knowledge is specified by the relative clause 'that he possessed', it requires the definite article. It should be 'The little knowledge'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Don't talk to / (b) him, he always / (c) remains in temper / (d) these days. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct idiomatic expression is 'in a temper', not 'in temper'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He boasts of / (b) having good knowledge / (c) of mathematics / (d) but everybody knows how far he is good at mathematics. / (e) No error.
options: but everybody knows how far he is good at mathematics.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'knowledge' is qualified by an adjective like 'good', it takes the indefinite article. It should be 'having a good knowledge'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) It was / (b) by a mistake / (c) that he caught / (d) her hand. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct idiomatic phrase is 'by mistake', without any article.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) These orders of / (b) the Manager / (c) may put the lives of / (d) two thousand workers in a danger. / (e) No error.
options: two thousand workers in a danger.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'in danger', without the indefinite article 'a'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) I inspired him / (b) to take the heart / (c) in all adverse situations / (d) and deserve to be called a real hero. / (e) No error.
options: and deserve to be called a real hero.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct idiom is 'take heart' (meaning to gain courage), without the article 'the'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) In my opinion it is not the failures / (b) that have made / (c) him lose the heart but the lack of / (d) emotional support. / (e) No error.
options: In my opinion it is not the failures
him lose the heart but the lack of
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct idiom is 'lose heart' (meaning to become discouraged), without the article 'the'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The most happy / (b) marriage would be / (c) a union of a deaf / (d) man to a blind woman. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The superlative form of 'happy' is 'happiest', not 'most happy'. It should be 'The happiest'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) John suggested to / (b) his brothers that they should / (c) go to the school regularly / (d) and do their home work sincerely. / (e) No error.
options: and do their home work sincerely.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When referring to the institution of school for the purpose of education, no article is used. It should be 'go to school regularly'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) After returning / (b) from the jail, he has abandoned / (c) all the criminal activities and is determined / (d) to lead a simple life. / (e) No error.
options: from the jail, he has abandoned
all the criminal activities and is determined
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'jail' is used to denote the institution/punishment rather than the physical building, no article is used. It should be 'from jail'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He was an atheist / (b) but now-a-days he goes to the church / (c) and offers prayers / (d) for hours. / (e) No error.
options: but now-a-days he goes to the church
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'church' is used for the purpose of worship, no article is used. It should be 'goes to church'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) His father / (b) forbade him to go / (c) to cinema / (d) late at night. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When referring to the entertainment venue, the definite article is required. It should be 'to the cinema'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The fact that the compact car / (b) is better than / (c) conventional cars has / (d) been proved by its sales. / (e) No error.
options: The fact that the compact car
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Conventional cars' is used in a general sense, requiring no article.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) There was little / (b) milk in the bottle and she gave it / (c) to the baby when it / (d) started weeping. / (e) No error.
options: milk in the bottle and she gave it
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Little milk' correctly implies a small, insufficient quantity, fitting the context.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He leads / (b) a very busy life / (c) so he goes everywhere / (d) by a car. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Modes of transport using 'by' do not take an article. It should be 'by car'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Thanks to an insight / (b) and persistence of the local doctor / (c) hundreds of victims have been / (d) able to resume a normal life. / (e) No error.
options: and persistence of the local doctor
able to resume a normal life.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Because 'insight' is specified by the phrase 'of the local doctor', it requires the definite article. It should be 'Thanks to the insight'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) In a hour's time / (b) when I had finished the work / (c) I got up and / (d) slipped out unnoticed. / (e) No error.
options: when I had finished the work
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound (silent 'h'), so it requires the indefinite article 'an'. It should be 'In an hour's time'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He uses / (b) the mock-heroic / (c) style to depict / (d) a violence. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Violence' is an uncountable abstract noun and does not take the indefinite article 'a'. It should be 'violence'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) People in Darwin / (b) had become so accustomed to / (c) cyclone warnings / (d) that few of them paid any attention to the radio warnings which began this morning. / (e) No error.
options: that few of them paid any attention to the radio warnings which began this morning.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Cyclone warnings' is used in a general sense, requiring no article.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) One should / (b) be true to one's promises / (c) in order to earn / (d) name and fame in the life / (e) No error.
options: name and fame in the life
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'life' is used in a general, abstract sense, no article is used. It should be 'in life'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The seed / (b) of all the modern amenities / (c) lies in / (d) the science. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'science' is used as a general field of study, it does not take the definite article. It should be 'in science'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) 'Music is science / (b) but singing is an art' / (c) said the / (d) music teacher. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When a singular countable noun represents a class or category, it requires an article. It should be 'Music is a science'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) We should spend / (b) a good part of the day / (c) in out of door activities and games / (d) because staying indoors all the time is bad for health. / (e) No error.
options: a good part of the day
in out of door activities and games
because staying indoors all the time is bad for health.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct compound adjective is hyphenated: 'out-of-door' or simply 'outdoor'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He should mix / (b) his authority with little / (c) of courtesy / (d) and common sense. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: To convey a positive meaning (some amount), 'a little' should be used instead of 'little' (which means hardly any).

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) It is a pity / (b) that the son of millionaire / (c) should indulge / (d) in stealing. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Millionaire' is a singular countable noun and requires an article. It should be 'son of a millionaire'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) This is / (b) the most important / (c) question which you have / (d) to prepare very carefully. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Brahmaputra is / (b) one of the longest rivers / (c) that originate / (d) in the Himalayas. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Names of rivers take the definite article 'The'. It should be 'The Brahmaputra is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The Ganges / (b) is for North India / (c) what Krishna / (d) is for South India / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: For parallel structure and correct grammar, names of rivers require the definite article. It should be 'what the Krishna is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The first European / (b) sailor to come to India / (c) in modern times / (d) was Vasco-di-Gama. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. (Note: 'Vasco-da-Gama' is the standard spelling, but 'Vasco-di-Gama' is treated as the proper noun provided in the source text).

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The trees in a forest / (b) must be properly counted and numbered / (c) and proper entries be made / (d) in the register. / (e) No error.
options: must be properly counted and numbered
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When referring to a specific, known forest contextually, or forests in general, 'the forest' is more appropriate. However, 'a forest' is grammatically acceptable. A stricter error is often (D) 'the register' -> 'a register' or (A) 'The trees in the forest'. Let's mark (A) with 'the forest' as the intended correction for specificity.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The principal / (b) asked the girls to return / (c) to the hostel before / (d) the sunset. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Times of day like 'sunset', 'sunrise', 'dawn', and 'dusk' do not take the definite article when used in this general sense. It should be 'before sunset'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He found / (b) himself in a trouble / (c) when he saw no / (d) rickshaw outside the station. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Trouble' is an uncountable noun in this context. The correct phrase is 'in trouble', without the article 'a'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He said / (b) that he did not feel / (c) any need to discuss / (d) the episode in the detail. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct idiomatic phrase is 'in detail', without the definite article 'the'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) In the conclusion / (b) it may be safely asserted that / (c) the poet preaches some / (d) moral implicity. / (e) No error.
options: it may be safely asserted that
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct transitional phrase is 'In conclusion', without the definite article 'the'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) All the staffs / (b) of this office hold the view / (c) that Mr. Sinha is a very wise / (d) and an intelligent officer. / (e) No error.
options: of this office hold the view
that Mr. Sinha is a very wise
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Staff' is a collective noun and is generally uncountable. It should be 'All the staff'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The man / (b) is the only creature / (c) that is endowed with / (d) the power of speech. / (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'man' is used to represent the human species as a whole, it is used without any article. It should be 'Man is the only creature'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) It is very difficult / (b) to point out the number of / (c) the creatures living / (d) on earth. / (e) No error.
options: to point out the number of
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When referring to creatures in a general, non-specific sense, the definite article 'the' should be omitted. It should be 'creatures living'.
